title: SCN Egg Extraction Protocol
author: Casey A Schlenker
materials: Let the cycle run and complete

steps.title: Prepare Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Filter soil cores to remove debris and prepare for extraction.

substeps.instruction: Pour a soil sample onto a mesh screen placed over a small plastic bin.
Gently break up large pieces by rolling cores against the mesh; do not crush to avoid squishing nematodes.
Discard rocks and large organic material (sticks, plant matter).
Brush the mesh with a scrub brush to remove sticking dirt.
Mix the filtered sample well and return it to its Ziploc bag/container.
Thoroughly brush the bin into a trash can to prevent cross-contamination.
Repeat for all remaining samples.

steps.title: Prepare Beakers and Tubes
steps.instruction: Set up containers for the elutriation process.

substeps.instruction: Fill 50 numbered 1 L beakers with 500 mL of water.
Add 100 cm3 of soil to each beaker (bringing total volume to 600 mL), adding samples in order from lowest to highest number.
Label 50 tubes (2 flats) with sample information in the same order as the beakers.

steps.title: Perform Elutriation
steps.instruction: Extract samples using the elutriator and nested sieves.

substeps.instruction: Place a 20 mesh sieve at an angle on top of a 60 mesh sieve on each elutriator collection funnel.
Set the elutriator timer to 5:00 minutes.
Press START before dumping samples to prevent loss.
Wash samples into elutriator cones using a water bottle.
Rinse the 20 sieve above the 60 sieve and discard material remaining in the 20 sieve.
Rinse the collected sample from the 60 sieve (kept at an angle) into the corresponding 50 mL tube.
Repeat for all samples, rinsing the mesh and funnel between each; store tubes in a refrigerator until grinding.

steps.title: Grind Cysts and Collect Eggs
steps.instruction: Mechanically crush cysts to release eggs using a drill press.

substeps.instruction: Set up nested sieves in a tub within the sink: a 500 sieve at an angle on the bottom, a 200 sieve on top of the 500, and a 60 PVC grinding sieve on top of the 200.
Pour one soil sample into a cup, fill with water, and pour into the 60 grinding sieve (swirl the cup first to remove sand).
Use a drill press with a stopper bit assembly to crush cysts in the 60 sieve, releasing eggs into the 200/500 sieves below.
Rinse repeatedly while gently grinding until only coarse sand remains in the 60 sieve.
Thoroughly rinse the 200 sieve material while holding it above the 500 sieve, then remove and discard the 200 sieve material.
Rinse the material caught in the 500 sieve (kept at an angle) into the correct tube using a water bottle.
Fill any empty space in the tube up to the 30 mL mark with water; do not exceed 30 mL.
Rinse the funnel to ensure all eggs are collected.
Rinse sieves and funnel and repeat for remaining samples.
Store samples in the refrigerator and stain within the same day to prevent hatching.

steps.title: Stain Egg Samples
steps.instruction: Apply egg stain and heat-fix the samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of egg stain by combining 0.35 g Acid Fusion Powder, 250 mL Lactic Acid, and 750 mL DH2O.
Pipette 3 mL of egg stain into each tube using a serpentine or left-to-right/front-to-back pattern.
Pour six egg samples into six labeled 400 mL beakers (1-6).
Rinse tubes completely with a distilled water bottle, ensuring the liquid volume in the beakers does not exceed 50 mL.
Microwave beakers in two batches of three for 90 seconds each.
Ensure samples boil for exactly 30 seconds for the stain to set (if processing only 1-2 samples, observe and time the boil for 30 seconds; do not microwave for 90 seconds).
Pour stained samples back into correct tubes, rinsing beakers with distilled water.
Fill empty space in tubes with water up to the 50 mL mark.
Repeat for all remaining samples, cleaning beakers between sets.

steps.title: Count Eggs
steps.instruction: Quantify eggs using a dissecting microscope.

substeps.instruction: Pour a stained sample into a 400 mL beaker with a stir bar.
Dilute the sample to 100 mL by adding 50 mL of water and stir on a stir plate.
Pipette 5 mL of the stirred sample into a counting dish.
Count eggs and empty shells within the engraved area of the dish using a dissecting microscope.
Multiply the count by 2 (since the engraved area is 1/2 of the total dish area) to get the number of eggs in the 5 mL sample.
Multiply the eggs per 5 mL by the dilution factor (typically 20) to calculate total eggs per 100 cm3 of soil.
Record eggs/5mL, dilution factor, and total eggs per 100 cm3 of soil.
Discard sample and rinse beaker between samples; repeat for all samples.

steps.title: Sucrose Flotation and Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Separate eggs from debris using sucrose solution and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Rinse tubes to remove silt and sugar; rinse sieves with distilled water and rinse into correct tubes.
Pour 45% sucrose solution into each tube up to the 45 mL mark.
Use a stirring utensil to suspend all material, rinsing the utensil between tubes.
Centrifuge tubes for 1 minute at 1500 rpm (9 Acc/7 Decc) (setting 2), ensuring even weight distribution.
Remove samples and use a syringe to extract water from the tubes without disturbing the sediment at the bottom.
Prepare four 500 sieves at an angle in the sink.
Select 4 egg samples, ensure equal liquid volumes, and centrifuge at 2800 rpm for 5 minutes (9 Acc/7 Decc) (setting 1).
Immediately after centrifugation, remove samples without disturbing them.
Pour liquid from tubes into corresponding 500 sieves, ensuring the plug at the base is not disturbed.
Thoroughly wash each sample in the sieves.
